keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Magdeburg row; its Holy Roman Empire shape draws the land as imperial). The page lists the state 'c. 1180 onward' as the city of Magdeburg, the bulk of the Magdeburg Börde, the Jerichow Land, and exclaves including Halle, Oebisfelde and Jüterbog, and gives no area or border. The circles are the researcher's, centred on the named places. Halle 'became a part of the Archbishopric of Magdeburg in the 10th century and remained so until 1680' (Halle page); Jüterbog was 'not incorporated into the Magdeburg diocese until 1157' (Jüterbog page).

region.text: the city of Magdeburg, the bulk of the Magdeburg Börde, the Jerichow Land and the exclaves Halle, Oebisfelde and Jüterbog

ledger.note: 1180: the archbishops become princes of the Empire. 'The archiepiscopal and cathedral temporalities gained imperial immediacy' on the breakup of the Duchy of Saxony; Archbishop Wichmann was rewarded for siding with the emperor and was 'the first to add the title secular prince' (Wichmann became 'the first Magdeburg prince-archbishop' in 1180 per his page). The page lists the land 'c. 1180 onward'; it does not say how much of it was held in 1180 exactly. The infobox lists 'Conquered Jüterbog' with the years 1157 and 1180; the Wichmann page says that in 1157 he allied with Albert the Bear to 're-conquer and Germanise the cities of Brandenburg and Jüterbog'.

1503: Halle becomes a capital alongside Magdeburg (infobox); Moritzburg at Halle was built 1484-1503 as the archbishops' residence (Halle page). The 1478 'Subdued Halle' of the infobox is not on the Halle page and is not drawn.

1635: the see passes to a Saxon prince. 'At the Peace of Prague, the archbishopric went to August, Duke of Saxe-Weissenfels'; the page's 'Saxon prince' who died in 1680 is presumably he, though it does not name him there. No land moves.

1648: Jüterbog passes to Saxony. At the Peace of Westphalia the Magdeburg archbishopric was promised to Brandenburg-Prussia 'but the town of Jüterbog passed to Saxony' (Jüterbog page); the Magdeburg page says only that the Treaty of Westphalia 'promised the succession to Brandenburg-Prussia'.

ledger.note: 1680: secularised by Brandenburg. 'When the Saxon prince died in 1680, the archbishopric was secularised by Brandenburg'; it became the Duchy of Magdeburg, 'a hereditary monarchy in personal union with Brandenburg'. The Halle page: 'The Margraviate of Brandenburg annexed Halle, together with Magdeburg, as the Duchy of Magdeburg.'

wars.name: Brandenburg domination of the see
wars.outcome: Günther I (1277-79) 'hardly escaped a serious war' with Margrave Otto IV; the Brandenburgers then forced Günther I and Bernhard III to resign and installed Eric of Brandenburg (1282/83-1295).

notes: Four pages opened (budget 2-5). The archdiocese dates from 968 (Synod of Ravenna 967), but the page gives the temporal state only from 1180, so the dossier starts then; earlier temporalities (Halle from the 10th century) are not drawn. The infobox 'Conquered Jüterbog 1157-1180' reads as the conquest of 1157 (Wichmann and Jüterbog pages), and the region is drawn from 1180 only. The page gives no area; the circles around Magdeburg, Jerichow, Halle, Oebisfelde and Jüterbog are the researcher's. Halberstadt, administered by the Magdeburg archbishops from 1480 (page), is not drawn because the page gives no end date or extent and Halberstadt has no dossier. Not settled: the 1478 'Subdued Halle' (infobox only; the Halle page is silent), the Sigismund 1552/1557 succession inconsistency, and the exact extent of the Jerichow Land and Börde.
